A B S T R A C T
The 1-(4-carboxyphenyl)-5-mercapto-1 h-tetrazole (CMHT) as a novel leveler for the overfilling of micro-blind
vias was investigated in acidic copper electroplating. The synergistic effect between CMHT and other addi-
tives were confirmed through chronoamperometry, cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance spec-
troscopy. The results showed a convection-dependent interaction between the CMHT and suppressor
(propyleneoxide (PO)-ethylene oxide (EO)-propylene oxide (PO), named PEP). Metallographic section testing
demonstrated that the CMHT not only have excellent microvia filling performances, but also only have 19.1 μm
thin surface Cu for micro blind vias with a diameter of 150 µm and a depth of 80 µm by the electrodepositing 60
min of 2 A/dm<sup>2</sup>. The quantum chemical calculations experiments revealed also that the CMHT parallel orien-
tation of the benzene ring and tetrazole heterocycle can enhance the effective adsorption area. The obtained
results from electrochemical test and quantum chemical calculations were in reasonably good agreement
1. Introduction
Copper plating process is widely applied in PCB and TSV industries
due to its excellent conductivity properties and low cost. Currently,
several important electronic interconnection applications encompass
processes such as electroless copper plating, blind via plating, and
through-hole plating. A significant issue associated with blind via
plating is the relatively thick copper layer on the surface, which prevent
effective and complete filling of the blind vias. On the other hand, the
miniaturization requirements of 3D packagings force manufacturers to
adopt multiple layers wiring interconnection structure to reducing the
interconnect line length and corresponding signal loss. In other words,
the vertical copper interconnection without void or seam can improve
the signal transmission rate and saving the installation components area
for PCB miniaturization [1–4].
In order to achieve high filling performance by CuSO -based elec
trolyte systems, the leveler have become the fundamental choice for via
fill applications due to it can prevent premature sealing of holes [5–8].
Typically, when using amine-containing glycidyl ethers as leveler, ad
vantages such as improved surface appearance and void-free filling of
blind vias are observed. However, these levelers are associated with a
slower copper filling rate and can result in excessively thick copper
layers on the surface. For example, the depth of the diameter of micro
blind is about 100um and the surface copper is generally 20 ~ 25 μm,
which is not easy to prepare fine circuit. In contrast, compounds such as
imidazole and polyepoxides, when utilized as levelers, have demon
strated advantages including a rapid filling rate for blind vias and a
thinner copper layer on the surface [5–10]. The CMHT has a relatively
small molecular weight and it contains thiol groups (−SH) and nitrogen-
containing heterocycles. Considering the structure of CMHT tetrazoles is
similar to imidazole as shown in Fig. 1, therefore, it is necessary to study
the conditions for obtaining excellent blind hole filling effect by con-
trolling the plating temperature, selecting appropriate current density
and time, and making the additives in the plating solution have a high
synergistic effect.

frequency range of 100 kHz–0.01 Hz at a steady potential of −0.65 V
versus SMSE.

2.3. Calculation methods
The molecular structures of CMHT and its isomer were optimized
using the B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) method with Gaussian 9 software. This
optimization was performed in accordance with front-line molecular
orbital theory [11,12], taking into account both the lowest unoccupied
molecular orbital (LUMO) and the highest occupied molecular orbital
(HOMO) [13,14,15]. The Forcite module was adopted to investigate the
interaction between the Cu (1 1 1) surface and CMHT using Material
Studio Software. In addition, molecular dynamics properties such as
radius of gyration, radial distribution function and diffusion coefficient
were analyzed for CMHT in the aqueous phase at a temperature of 298 K.
The COMPASS II force field was utilized to optimize the size and
simulate the adsorption process of CMHT. The kinetic parameters were
set to include canonical ensemble with a time step of 1.0 fs and total
simulation time of 500 ps containing 500 water molecules which added
to the box.
